_readme: Machine-readable project status. Read this at the start of a session to orient; update it at the end of any task that changes what's built or what's broken. Prose belongs in the docs — this file is the ledger. Status values: not_started | in_progress | complete | blocked.
current_phase: Two rigs now. ANDY/M2: verified and calibrated 2026-08-12, but marine Ch 16 is NOT receivable at his location with the stock antenna indoors (hardware.md 4) - unchanged, and his thresholds still came from a 100 ms median that may sit inside a 20 ms tail (bringup-log 2026-09-10). PARKER/UFO202: the working rig. Radio IN THE WINDOW at volume 13/31 with a Nagoya NA-773, gating on the voice band 300-3400 Hz since 2026-09-10 (decisions D22) at floor -39.8, thresholds -28.9/-32.9. Real marine audio, real ASR and real Coast Guard traffic are in the database. 2026-09-15 was the first long live watch: 6 h 37 min, 2 transmissions, both captured, both in the operator's ear log, no fragments, no queue drops - but only 2 events, so it credits neither the antenna nor anything else. Per the operator Ch 16 here is normally VERY quiet and 9/10 was the atypical session, so capture RATE is the metric, not totals, and long silences are expected. Two things are now waiting on a decision rather than on hardware: volume 13 leaves zero clipping headroom (2 of 2 loud transmissions touched the ceiling on 9/15), and the operator plans to move the rig closer to the water, which makes it a new site needing its own calibrate.py run (D11). Still unmeasured and still the biggest gap: nobody has hand-labelled data/labels.jsonl or run evaluate.py, so the two deliberately-unfixed findings (est_snr_db does not measure intelligibility; the hysteresis window straddles squelch-open hiss) remain guesses rather than measured decisions. 2026-09-23 was the big session: 9 h 25 min, 18 transmissions, 13 with words, none fragmented, and PUSHOVER NOW WORKS END TO END for the first time (scripts/notify_transmissions.py, a bring-up tool - one push per transmission with transcript and a LAN audio link, 4-13 s behind the radio; credentials live in ~/.vhfwatch-pushover.env outside the repo). Three findings came out of it and all three are in known_issues or the bring-up log: (1) capture DIED SILENTLY at about 17:31 and nothing noticed for ~50 minutes, which is the worst-outcome failure mode observed for real and makes a capture heartbeat the top Phase 4 item; (2) every clean transcript of the day was Coast Guard and every unreadable one was the small craft this project exists to hear, which is the strongest argument yet for the water-side relocation; (3) a COMPLETE Coast Guard assistance case ran start to finish and produced ZERO detections because no watchword was spoken - Tier 2 was off (no VHFWATCH_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY), so replaying 17:21-17:31 with the classifier on is now the single most valuable pending experiment. UPDATE 2026-10-09: the live rig is now the MCS 2000 STATION RIG (pin-11 tap, built and calibrated this day - floor -91.3 dBFS, first transmission 54 dB SNR and transcribed exactly), running on TELEGRAM (decisions D26): every transmission arrives as one message with the recording and transcript together, health notices arrive silently, and the capture watchdog (D24) plus the 6-hour no-transmission alert are armed. Of the 9/23 next-session list: volume 12 is MOOT (the tap is pre-volume, so the knob cannot affect capture); the USB dropout's cause is still UNDIAGNOSED but is now caught by the watchdog instead of going unnoticed; replaying the 17:21-17:31 assistance case with Tier 2 enabled is STILL the most valuable pending experiment; the water-side move is undecided. The unattended-week host is decided (D27): an x86 N100 mini PC with INTEL wifi, Ubuntu Server headless, UFO202 staying at the station, power loss acceptable. STILL BLOCKING an unattended week: daily self-test push, systemd units, per-stage heartbeats beyond capture, and retry of a failed notification across station-wifi drops. The first live transmission through Telegram has not yet been observed. Tier 2 is still off (no VHFWATCH_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY).

phase_0_skeleton.notes: Exit criterion verified 2026-07-30. The Phase 0 refuse-non-16kHz behavior was replaced in Phase 2 by automatic resampling; archival WAV was replaced in Phase 3 by Opus+AAC (WAV remains the no-ffmpeg fallback).

phase_1_transcription_detection.notes: All code items landed 2026-08-10: asr/ (mlx + faster_whisper behind Transcriber, warmup at startup), detect/ (hallucination gates, watchword matcher with phonetic guards per D14, LLM classifier with hard graceful degradation, severity resolution per architecture §5.5), incidents/correlator.py, scripts/replay.py + evaluate.py. 113 tests pass; ruff and mypy --strict clean. 2026-09-23 produced the best available test case for Tier 2: a COMPLETE Coast Guard assistance case (17:21-17:31 local, 13 transmissions - vessel hailing unanswered, GPS position requested, anchor advised, vessel description and cell number taken, TowBoatUS brought in, formal sign-off) that generated ZERO detections, because no watchword was ever spoken - the emergency is legible only from the Coast Guard's QUESTIONS. Tier 2 was off all day (no VHFWATCH_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY). Replaying that window with the classifier enabled is a measured answer to whether Tier 2 earns its place, against real traffic rather than a fixture. REMAINING (corpus-dependent, not code): hand-label data/labels.jsonl, run evaluate.py for a precision/recall baseline, and the base.en/small.en/medium.en WER comparison. 2026-10-09: faster-whisper has now run on 20 real transmissions and is fit for the x86 host (decisions D25) - 3.2x realtime vs MLX's 9.1x, but only 2 of 20 transcripts identical, so the engines are NOT interchangeable and any WER baseline must record which engine produced it. faster-whisper RECOVERED content MLX dropped entirely (including a position: 'off of Lopez Island'), and also produced hallucination loops where MLX correctly stayed silent - max_repeat_tokens=3 catches those, which makes the hallucination gate load-bearing for the deployment engine.

phase_2_live_audio.notes: All CODE items landed 2026-08-10. HARDWARE: docs/hardware.md §5 steps 3, 4 and 5 now PASS on the M2 rig (2026-08-12) — device selection, channel slice, level, and a clean 30 s recording. Thresholds in Andy's config.toml are measured, not guessed. REMAINING for 'complete': §5 step 6, the 30-minute segment-count exit criterion during busy traffic. Steps 1 (hear traffic by ear) and the §2.1 radio programming spot-check were skipped and should be done before trusting any negative result. Added scripts/level_meter.py this session — calibrate.py is a batch tool and the wrong shape for setting a trim by hand. 2026-09-15 on PARKER's rig: a 6 h 37 min unattended-ish live run stayed healthy end to end (2 transmissions, both segmented and transcribed, 0 drops), which is the longest continuous live run so far, but it does NOT satisfy the exit criterion — that asks for a segment count during BUSY traffic and the channel was near-silent. It needs a busy session, which on this channel cannot be scheduled.

phase_3_alerting_and_record.notes: Landed 2026-08-10: console/macos/pushover channels behind AlertChannel, router (alert-once-then-update, dedupe, escalation re-alert; no-ack escalation via Pushover priority 2 per D16), offline-complete notification body, share tokens (hash-only storage, access logged), FastAPI web app as a separate process with all §5.10 routes, canvas waveform per D15, honest uncertainty rendering, feedback + annotations. Exit criterion (replayed mayday → Pushover → phone) is still formally untested, but 2026-09-23 proved the Pushover leg for real: live transmissions pushed to the operator's iPhone with transcript and a tappable LAN audio link, 4-13 s after each transmission ended, via scripts/notify_transmissions.py. That script is a BRING-UP TOOL, not the alert path - it notifies on every transmission rather than on detections, and it pushed a transcript the pipeline had REJECTED without saying so, which is fine for an ear-log comparison and misleading in anything operational. Two limits found while wiring it: share-token scope is per-incident, so per-transmission audio links have to reuse one token minted against some incident; and phone-reachable links need the web app bound beyond loopback with base_url set to the LAN IP (done 2026-09-23, reverted at shutdown).

phase_4_reliability.notes: Watchdog, heartbeats, no-transmission alert, daily self-test, systemd units, x86 Linux verification. Noise-floor drift warning already exists in the pipeline tick; the rest is unbuilt. /health is honest about this gap. TOP ITEM as of 2026-09-23, promoted by a real silent capture death (see known_issues): a CAPTURE HEARTBEAT that asserts audio frames are still arriving, not merely that the process is alive. Sample-count time falling behind wall clock is a direct, cheap signal and was visible in the data 50 minutes before anything warned. The drift warning is NOT a substitute - it fires once and only when the estimate moves, which needs audio to move it. The check that actually caught it was opening the input device rather than reading a cached device list.

phase_5_tuning.notes: Incident review with Parker, threshold retuning against real feedback labels, lead-time statistics.

corpus_collection.notes: BLOCKED for MARINE audio as of 2026-08-12: Ch 16 is not receivable at Andy's house with the stock antenna indoors. Fire traffic rebroadcast on the radio's 'Forge ch 3' memory IS receivable and will be recorded to data/corpus-fire/ (kept separate so it never contaminates marine tuning, labelling or evaluate.py runs). Fire/EMS audio is more sensitive than marine chatter - addresses and patient details are plausible - so do not share it as freely as the docs encourage for marine corpus. Marine corpus needs a better antenna or a better-sited recording location.

bringup_log.notes: Entries through 2026-10-01, now three rigs. Parker's knob POSITION is still not written down (the knob is taped, the position is not recorded), so a bump or a re-tape cannot be undone from the docs. Andy's knobs are not taped at all.

parker_mcs2000_station.interface: Behringer UFO202 (LINE position; PHONO adds ~40 dB + RIAA)
parker_mcs2000_station.radio: Motorola MCS 2000, City of Bellingham asset 2168, spare, modification authorised by the comms chief for THIS radio only
parker_mcs2000_station.tap: HLN6412A accessory connector, pin 11 FIL AUD OUT (pre-volume) and pin 10 ANALOG GND, TE 1658537-2 sockets soldered to an RCA pigtail into UFO202 left
parker_mcs2000_station.notes: Built and verified 2026-10-09; full procedure and gotchas in docs/hardware.md 3.9, session story in the bring-up log. Channel is zone WDBAND / WCG16. Pin numbering was PROVEN, not assumed, by metering the plug's factory jumpers (1-2 adjacent, 4-9 five apart) plus the red IGNITION wire on 15. Pre-volume tap means the radio volume knob cannot affect capture - the single biggest improvement over the handheld rigs. OPEN ITEMS: ground-loop isolator removed during debugging and never reinstalled (current numbers are direct); calibrated on BATTERY with mains untested (the old rig gained 8.9 dB of hum on mains per D21, unknown here); and the HLN6412A housing was opened and reseated repeatedly on build day, so tug-test the contacts before trusting a long unattended run.

andy_m2.notes: Verified and calibrated 2026-08-12. Radio on M2 INPUT 2, so use_channel = 1 (input 1 carries Andy's XLR mic). Connected via Thunderbolt dock, which measured 12 dB quieter in the voice band than direct USB-C - keep the dock. SETTLED GAIN STAGING: radio volume 3/4, M2 input 2 trim 90 deg, which inverts hardware.md 3.5's default for a measured reason (docs/decisions.md D18). At that setting: speech peaks -7.6 dBFS, zero clipped samples, idle floor -68.1 dBFS - measured twice either side of a failed re-staging experiment and reproducible to 0.3 dB by hand. 60 Hz pickup on the idle line is self-cancelling and deliberately unfiltered (D17). Knobs still need physically taping. No squelch control on this radio; no macOS input slider exists for the M2.

parker_ufo202.notes: CURRENT VALUES (in config) are BAND-LIMITED, 300-3400 Hz at 20 ms windows, measured 2026-09-10 with the laptop on mains: floor -39.8, open -28.9, close -32.9 (decisions D22, bringup-log 2026-09-10). They are NOT comparable to the full-band figures they replaced. VERIFIED against real transmissions 2026-09-15: two events, both segmented cleanly and closed by hang_time, speech at -17.1 and -13.3 dBFS RMS against the -28.9 open threshold, and nine half-hourly idle readings spanning battery and mains power stayed within 1.3 dB of the calibrated floor with no drift warning. SUPERSEDED HISTORY: calibrated 2026-09-07, then recalibrated the same evening after the radio was moved into the window and the volume dropped 17->13 to stop clipping (full-band floor -41.1, open -34.1, close -38.1, the D19 offsets). Note calibrate.py was run THREE times: the first run showed a 3.8 dB p90 spread that sits under its 6 dB instability warning and would have put close_threshold within 0.2 dB of p90; two repeats gave p90 == median exactly. Do not paste a single run into config. Radio on RCA left, use_channel = 0. Level set by the radio volume knob alone (the UFO202 has no input trim — the front knob is headphone output only) and TAPED, but the knob POSITION was never written down. Speech peaks -9.2 dBFS. CLIPPING IS NOT SETTLED: on 2026-09-15 both loud transmissions of the session peaked at -0.16 and -0.08 dBFS, tripping clip_warn_dbfs (-0.5), with 0.03-0.05% of samples within 1 dB of full scale - no audible distortion and no effect on transcription, but no margin either. Volume 12 is the candidate (speech averages -13 dBFS against a -28.9 open threshold, so a step down is unlikely to cost detections) and requires re-running calibrate.py. Decide between sessions, not during one. Floor -38.3 dBFS with p90 == median (0.0 dB spread over 30 s) — rock steady, and owner-confirmed as the operating baseline (radio in normal monitoring state, nothing transmitting), but 30 dB above the M2 rig's -68.1 with the squelch closed on BOTH rigs, cause not yet diagnosed. RULED OUT 2026-10-09: the interface is a UFO202, not a UCA202 as every doc said until that date (both enumerate as USB Audio CODEC), and the UFO202 has a LINE/PHONO switch whose phono preamp would add ~35-40 dB and explain the gap exactly - but the switch was verified on LINE before being touched. The gap is not that. Thresholds deliberately deviate from the usual offsets: open = floor + 7 (not +10, because measured variability is zero), hysteresis 4 dB (not 6, because a 6 dB close threshold would land exactly on the floor and the gate would never close). See docs/decisions.md D19 — this is a provisional setting with an open defect behind it, not a settled property of the rig.

known_issues.description: PARTIAL 2026-10-09: the capture heartbeat (Phase 4 item 1) is BUILT - pipeline.capture_watchdog raises CaptureStalled and exits non-zero when no audio FRAMES arrive for [health].capture_stall_s (default 30), so systemd Restart=always brings the process back with a fresh stream (decisions D24). Armed for live sources only and disarmed when ingest ends; 3 regression tests in tests/test_capture_watchdog.py, 147 tests pass, ruff and mypy --strict clean. WHAT IT DOES NOT COVER, and these are the remaining blockers for an unattended week: a radio powered off, tuned away, or with the antenna knocked loose all deliver perfectly good frames of silence - the "no transmission in N hours" alert is what catches those; the NO-TRANSMISSION ALERT is now built too (2026-10-09): the pipeline tick compares transmission count against [health].no_audio_alert_hours (default 6), fires ONCE per silent spell, re-arms when traffic returns, writes a health_event row, and sends via a new AlertChannel.send_health path on [alerting].channels_health at Pushover priority 0 - deliberately NOT the incident channels, because a dead USB cable must not bypass Do Not Disturb like a mayday (D12). 149 tests pass. STILL MISSING for an unattended week: the daily self-test push, systemd units, per-stage heartbeats for ASR/detection/alerting, and alert retry across the station wifi drops Parker expects.

BUILT AND WORKING 2026-10-09 - the THIRD rig is now the best audio chain the project has. A spare Motorola MCS 2000 at Parker's fire station, tapped at pin 11 FIL AUD OUT (pre-volume) on the HLN6412A accessory connector, into the UFO202 left channel. Measured: idle floor -91.3 dBFS band-limited (vs -39.8 on the handheld rig, ~50 dB quieter), idle spread 1.8 dB, speech p50 -52.9 / p99 -33.2, first live transmission 54.1 dB SNR with peak -13.5 and a word-perfect transcript. The volume-knob dependency and the clipping problem are both retired because the tap is pre-volume. Config updated: noise_floor_dbfs -91.3, open -83.5, close -87.5, site_name bellingham-station-mcs2000. THE BUILD FAILURE WORTH REMEMBERING: contacts pushed into the housing but not LATCHED sit near their pins without touching, couple capacitively, and pass a signal ~40 dB down - invisible in LINE mode and indistinguishable from a dead chain. Reseating fixed it. Two techniques came out of the debugging and are in hardware.md 3.9: flip the UFO202 to PHONO as a free 40 dB presence detector, and never trust a DMM on AC volts at a floating connector (one read a big jump on a dead line from hand capacitance and cost an hour). OPEN: the ground-loop isolator was removed during debugging and never reinstalled, so current numbers are direct; and calibration was done on BATTERY, untested on mains.

OBSERVED FOR REAL 2026-09-23, and it is the failure mode AGENTS.md calls the worst outcome: the UFO202 disappeared from the host (gone from audio_devices.py and from the USB bus) at about 17:31 local, and NOTHING NOTICED FOR ~50 MINUTES. The pipeline process stayed alive, logged nothing, and /health would have looked normal; the noise-floor drift warning did not fire until 18:24 because it only fires when the estimate MOVES, which needs audio. It was caught only by a session habit - a half-hourly 5 s check that OPENS the device directly and got ValueError: No input device matching USB Audio CODEC. At 18:24 a stalled buffer flushed and produced a bogus 1.8 s transmission stamped 17:36:33 (started_at is derived from sample counting, so a stalled stream drifts behind wall clock) transcribed as a hallucination on a -57.5 dBFS line; that row is annotated in the DB as not-real-audio and must be excluded from corpus, labelling and evaluate.py. Cause NOT established - cable, hub or dock power are the candidates and the rig was shut down before diagnosis. Phase 4 requirements this produces: (1) a capture heartbeat that asserts FRAMES ARE STILL ARRIVING rather than that the process lives - sample-count time falling behind wall clock is a direct and cheap signal; (2) the drift warning is not a substitute for (1); (3) probing the device by opening it, not reading a cached device list, is the check that actually worked and belongs in the product.

MEASURED 2026-09-23 on 18 real transmissions: every clean transcript of the day was a COAST GUARD transmission and every unreadable one ("!", repeated "!", or empty - 5 of 18) was the other side of a conversation, i.e. the small craft this project exists to hear. One clip (17:24:25) contains both in sequence - it opens "! !" for the vessel then transcribes the Coast Guard cleanly - same recording, same radio, same moment. Signal strength does not separate the two populations: 19.8 dB produced a full sentence while 25.7 dB with no_speech_prob 0.05 produced a single "!" across 11 seconds of audio the model was confident was speech. CONFIRMED BY EAR 2026-10-09: two transmissions at 58.7 and 57.8 dB SNR - the cleanest this project has recorded - were unreadable to BOTH ASR engines and to the operator listening live, who judged them a distant station. That is the first ear-confirmed case that an unreadable transcript is unintelligible AUDIO rather than a model failure, and it means a bigger model will not help this class - the information is not in the recording. est_snr_db should be read as 'how far above the noise floor', never 'how readable'. This reproduces the 2026-09-07 finding that est_snr_db does not measure intelligibility, with a much stronger case, and it argues for the water-side relocation over any model change - a bigger model cannot recover what the RF path destroyed. Vessel NAMES are the consistent casualty (one vessel came through as Sir Muggis / Sir budget / For budget / For budgets / For much assistance), which is precisely what identifies a boat in a real mayday.

UNTESTED as of 2026-09-15: whether the live pipeline recovers its audio capture stream after the host sleeps and wakes. Nothing in the code reopens the stream, and the only thing that would surface a dead stream is the noise-floor drift warning, which fires once and only when the estimate moves - it is not a heartbeat. Assume a sleep/wake cycle silently ends monitoring until someone verifies otherwise. Workaround used on 2026-09-15: run `caffeinate -i -w <pipeline pid>` for the session, which blocks idle sleep and exits with the pipeline; closing the lid still sleeps the machine regardless. Proper fix belongs to Phase 4 (heartbeats, watchdog, no-transmission alert).

The clips in audio-test-samples/ (and their 16 kHz conversions in data/corpus/) were recorded from the radio's speaker through a laptop mic, NOT through the line-in chain. They are useful only as smoke-test input for the pipeline. Do not tune segmenter thresholds against them, do not treat their noise floors (-60 to -77 dBFS) as representative, and do not use them for the Phase 1 WER comparison — wait for real line-in corpus audio.

RESOLVED 2026-09-07: real ASR has now run end to end on real radio audio (Parker's rig, ch 7 test transmission, mlx-whisper small.en). The pipeline segmented 2 transmissions, transcribed both, archived Opus, and wrote to the DB with 0 pre-ASR rejects, 0 post-ASR rejects and 0 queue drops. faster-whisper is still exercised only at import/signature level.

FIXED 2026-09-07, same day it was found (see the fix commit; regression tests in tests/test_asr.py and tests/test_hallucination.py, 122 tests pass, ruff and mypy --strict clean). Verified by re-running the pipeline over the recording that exposed it: the transcript with the NaN now logs transcript.checks_unrunnable and the one with a real value does not. ORIGINAL REPORT: on the first real ASR run, mlx-whisper returns avg_logprob as NaN (not missing) on many segments — 4 of 5 whisper segments in the ch 7 test. Consequences chain badly. (1) asr/base.py merge_segments duration-weights the values, so a SINGLE NaN segment makes the merged avg_logprob NaN for the whole transmission. (2) At the gate, detect/hallucination.py line 56 tests `t.avg_logprob is not None and t.avg_logprob < threshold`, and NaN < -1.0 is False, so the check silently passes — the `is not None` guard never fires because the value is NaN, not None. (3) Written to SQLite, NaN is stored as NULL, which is why the transcript row reads None and masks the cause. Net effect: the logprob half of the post-ASR hallucination gate is INERT, and in the observed case it failed open on the LOWER-quality of the two segments — the one with a spurious '!' token and a mangled position readback, i.e. exactly what it exists to catch. no_speech_prob still functions, so the gate is degraded rather than absent. AGENTS.md calls detect/hallucination.py load-bearing. Fix direction: treat NaN as MISSING (math.isnan) in merge_segments so it stops poisoning the merged score, and make the gate LOG that the logprob check could not run rather than passing silently. Note failing closed would be wrong here: NaN appeared on 4 of 5 segments, so rejecting on unknown logprob would discard most real transcripts — the project accepts missed detections but not blind ones, and an unrunnable check is an uncertainty to surface (the web app already renders honest uncertainty) rather than a reason to drop evidence. Needs a regression test with a NaN segment; no current test covers it, which is how this reached real audio.

First measured transcription quality on real radio audio (Parker's rig, 2026-09-07, small.en, chain 30 dB compromised): call signs, position minutes and persons-on-board counts were all corrupted. 'test station one' -> 'position one'; 'three six minutes north' dropped entirely; 'one two two degrees' -> 'one, two, two screens'; 'two one minutes west' -> 'one minute west'; 'Three persons on board' -> 'persons on board'. Degrees numbers survived ('four seven' -> '47'). This is a BASELINE on a known-bad audio chain, not a verdict on model choice — it should be re-measured after the 43 dB noise problem is diagnosed, and it is the first real input to the base.en/small.en/medium.en WER comparison. It also concretely validates the architecture's insistence that original audio stay reachable from every alert: a human hears the position correctly, the ASR does not.
LiveAudioSource's disconnect/reconnect path is untested against a real USB unplug — it needs a deliberate yank test during bring-up.

Parker's UFO202 rig is calibrated as of 2026-09-07 and its thresholds are measured, not guessed. Still unverified on that rig: §5 step 5 (no recording has been written to disk — the meter ran without --record), step 6 (segmentation against real traffic), and the radio's programming (channel, modulation, bandwidth, tone squelch are owner-confirmed on Andy's radio but NOT on Parker's). Calibration does not transfer between rigs (docs/decisions.md D11).

Pushover delivery is untested (needs VHFWATCH_PUSHOVER_TOKEN/USER and a phone). The Phase 3 exit criterion — alert deep link opens a playable incident record on a phone — has not been walked end to end.
The Tier 2 classifier prompt has never been evaluated against real traffic; llm_min_confidence=0.6 and the severity-resolution judgment calls in detect/detector.py are untuned defaults.
ASR model choice (base.en / small.en / medium.en) is unresolved pending measured WER on the real corpus. Config defaults to small.en.
The web app's 'dropped segments' honesty indicator is absent — nothing persists queue drops or pre-ASR rejects yet. Lands with Phase 4 health events.

Andy's M2 knobs are at the settled setting (radio volume 3/4, M2 input 2 trim 90 deg; docs/decisions.md D18) and re-verified, but are NOT physically taped. A bump silently invalidates open_threshold_db, and the pipeline's noise-floor drift warning is the only thing that would catch it.

The M2 measured 12 dB quieter in the voice band through the Thunderbolt dock than connected directly to the laptop on battery, with identical mains content. Reproducible but unexplained; suspected USB power-rail switching noise reaching the bus-powered interface. Keep the dock. Matters because it means the audio chain has a 12 dB failure mode triggered by nothing more than re-plugging a cable.

TX inhibit is unverified on Andy's monitoring NX-5200 and is deliberately untested, since testing it means transmitting. Do not press PTT on the monitoring radio. Modulation, bandwidth and tone squelch are owner-confirmed correct as of 2026-08-12.

Gain staging on the M2 rig inverts docs/hardware.md 3.5's default ordering, and this is measured, not preference: the 60 Hz interference is picked up on the cable downstream of the radio's volume knob, so the interface trim cannot improve SNR. Moving gain from radio to interface raised the idle floor from -68.4 to -38.0 dBFS and caused clipping. Radio high / trim low is correct here (docs/decisions.md D18). Anyone 'fixing' this back to 1/3 radio volume will silently break detection.

Parker's UFO202 rig measures a -38.3 dBFS noise floor against the M2 rig's -68.1 — a 30 dB gap between two rigs running the same radio model with the squelch closed on both, so it is a chain defect and not open-squelch hiss (an earlier reading of this data wrongly assumed the latter). The floor is extremely stable (p90 == median), and a 13 dB crest factor points at broadband amp or converter noise rather than a ground loop. Consequence: the gate sits near -31 instead of -58, so weak and distant stations are lost. Accepted provisionally by the rig's owner so the rig can be used now (AGENTS.md: missed detections are acceptable), but it is expected to be diagnosed, not filed away. The gain-staging hypothesis is FALSIFIED: Parker's volume knob is 17 of 0-31, BELOW Andy's 3/4 (~23), yet peak-to-floor is 29.1 dB against Andy's 60.5 dB — 31 dB less usable range with the radio turned DOWN further, so the radio's own amp is not the source and the noise enters downstream of the volume control (cable, UFO202, USB power, or charger). This makes the rig a second instance of D18, not its opposite: input_gain_db sits downstream of the noise and cannot improve SNR, and turning the radio UP would help but is capped near 3 dB by ADC headroom. That measurement was run 2026-09-07 and CLEARS the interface: UFO202 alone with nothing on its inputs reads -88.8 dBFS (p90 -88.7), its own converter floor and 20 dB below the entire M2 chain. Interface, USB power and host are eliminated; all ~50 dB enters from the radio side of the RCA cable. This does not exonerate the radio — noise injected into its output stage AFTER its volume control (a charger being the obvious candidate) would not scale with the knob and fits the data. Remaining split is charger vs radio output vs cable pickup; the charger A/B (battery-only, then charging) separates them in two 30-second runs. The rig is not inherently limited: a floor matching or beating Andy's is available in principle once the source is found. The charger A/B test (battery vs charging, idle vs during a transmission) is the cheapest next discriminator and has still not been run. See docs/decisions.md D19.

FIXED 2026-09-07 (see docs/decisions.md D20). phonetic_min_similarity raised 0.70 -> 0.85, and multi-word terms now require EVERY token to clear phonetic_min_token_similarity (0.80) against its counterpart rather than scoring the joined string. All ten observed false positives are silent, including three verbatim real transcripts, while every distress phrase still fires. The cost is recorded and deliberate: mated -> mayday (0.760) is now missed, which was D14 canonical example, because it scores BELOW my/made/monday at 0.800 and no threshold separates them. 139 tests pass; ruff and mypy --strict clean. ORIGINAL REPORT: found on the first real Ch 16 transmission ever processed: the phonetic watchword pass produces false positives on extremely common radio words. Measured against config/watchwords.example.toml: 'my' -> mayday (score 0.80), 'made' -> mayday (0.80), 'maybe' -> mayday (0.79), and 'going to' -> 'going down' (0.92). All are CRITICAL terms. Two distinct causes. (1) detect/watchwords.py applies phonetic_min_token_len (4) to the TERM's tokens, not to the MATCHED text, so a 2-character word like 'my' is allowed to match a 6-character term like 'mayday'; a length-ratio guard between term and matched token is missing. (2) Multi-word terms combine per-token scores into an average, so one exactly-matching token ('going') carries a garbage second token ('to' vs 'down') over the similarity floor; every token should have to clear its own bar. The suppress list catches specific cases ('monday') but a blocklist cannot scale to 'my'. Severity resolution limited the blast radius correctly - phonetic hits resolve to WATCH, not CRITICAL, per architecture 5.5 - but an incident was still opened with confidence 0.915. On a busy channel this would fire on a large fraction of all traffic, which is the exact failure D12 warns about: users trained to silence the app. AGENTS.md is explicit that missed detections are acceptable and false positives are not. Note this is precisely the evidence D14 named as its revisit condition, arriving from real audio rather than from evaluate.py.

FIXED 2026-09-10 in code and config (docs/decisions.md D22), and the ground-loop isolator was deliberately NOT bought (D23): the hum exists only while the radio output is muted - it collapses ~28 dB the instant the squelch opens (60 Hz -36.4 to -64, 120 Hz -32.3 to -60) - so it never reaches the audio the transcriber sees, and transcription quality here is set by the RF path rather than the laptop supply. What is given up: band-limited idle floor -39.8 against an open threshold of -28.9 leaves about 11 dB of headroom where an isolator would restore ~13 dB, so a different laptop, outlet or added charger could eat the margin and jam the gate again. Re-run calibrate.py after ANY power-setup change; that is the 30-second early warning. The isolator becomes necessary when the rig runs unattended (Phase 4). FIXED 2026-09-10 in code and config (docs/decisions.md D22): the segmenter can now gate on a frequency band (segmenter.gate_band_hz, default [] = full-band so no existing rig changes; Parker sets [300.0, 3400.0]). The archived audio is never filtered - only the gate and noise-floor estimate see the band. Verified end to end by replaying the recording that jammed: it now produces 29.5 s and 2.2 s segments closed by hang_time, matching the two real transmissions, instead of one 120 s segment closed by max_duration. ORIGINAL REPORT: with the LAPTOP PLUGGED INTO MAINS, Parker's rig idles at -31.8 dBFS instead of -40.7 - 8.9 dB of supply hum, 84% of the energy in mains harmonics with 120 Hz dominant (full-wave rectified ripple, not the 60 Hz-dominant ambient pickup of D17). Unplugging the laptop restores -40.7 with p90 == median and drops 180 Hz by 45 dB. The hum is harmless to speech - it collapses ~28 dB the instant the squelch opens, exactly D17's mechanism - but at -31.8 the idle line sits ABOVE open_threshold_db (-34.1), so the segmenter gate would never close and Whisper would be fed continuous hum. See docs/decisions.md D21: D17's test (does the hum survive a transmission?) is necessary but not sufficient; the second question is whether the idle floor stays below the open threshold. calibrate.py gives NO hint - it reported a stable floor with p90 == median and no warning. Running the laptop on battery is a test-day fix only; permanent mains operation needs a 1:1 audio isolation transformer on the RCA line (~$15, hardware.md 3.5), which is now the SECOND independent measurement pointing there after the radio charger cost 7.4 dB on 2026-09-07.

PRELIMINARY 2026-09-10, do not cite as a result: the Nagoya NA-773 telescopic antenna is installed on Parker's rig and the first session captured 2 of 2-3 transmissions over 1h28m, both FULL-LENGTH with zero fragments, against a 7 Sep baseline of 2 of 8 with 2 of 3 captures being sub-0.6 s fragments. Only the antenna changed - same site, window position, volume 13 and channel - so it is a clean single-variable comparison. But TWO EVENTS IS NOT A RESULT: traffic was light, and a quiet channel produces the same numbers as a good antenna. Several more sessions are needed. The concurrent laptop-hum problem does not confound it, since that affects the audio floor rather than whether the radio hears anything.

BUG FIXED 2026-09-10, and it predates this session: scripts/calibrate.py measured 100 ms windows while the segmenter gates on segmenter.frame_ms (20 ms) windows. Short windows average less noise so their tail is far higher - the same idle line reads p90 -40.0 / max -39.9 at 100 ms but p90 -37.0 / max -34.9 at 20 ms, a 5 dB difference. Thresholds derived from the 100 ms median therefore sat INSIDE the 20 ms tail; the close threshold was crossed about 1.5 times a second, and since the gate closes only after hang_ms of CONTINUOUS quiet each crossing reset the timer and the gate never closed - every segment ran to max_duration_ms. calibrate.py now measures at frame_ms and derives thresholds from the TAIL rather than the median (close = loudest idle window + 2 dB, open = close + 4 dB), because what matters for closing is the loudest window the idle line produces, not its average. WARNING, NOT YET CHECKED: this affects full-band rigs too and was merely invisible while margins were wide. Andy's M2 close_threshold_db (-64.1) was derived as median + 4 dB from a 100 ms measurement and has never been checked against a 20 ms tail - it may be sitting inside one. Re-run calibrate.py on the M2 rig before trusting its segment durations.

DESIGN GAP found 2026-09-07 on 2h14m of real traffic: est_snr_db does not measure intelligibility, and on an FM receiver it cannot. Once squelch opens, the recovered audio LEVEL is constant regardless of signal strength - only its QUALITY degrades - so a metric based on level above the muted-line floor is decoupled from whether anything is readable. Concretely: a 17-second Coast Guard broadcast scored est_snr_db 16.3 dB and was UNINTELLIGIBLE to Whisper, which returned the single character '!' across raw, normalised and high-passed variants. The audio genuinely is speech-shaped - broadband, with the top 12 spectral bins holding 0.97% of the energy and an envelope modulation peak at 3.11 Hz, squarely syllabic - it is simply too degraded to read. Consequence: hallucination.min_snr_db (3.0) is a pre-ASR gate that every marginal transmission on this rig will pass, handing unreadable audio to a model this project documents as hallucinating confidently on noise. This time it emitted '!' rather than a sentence, which is luck rather than a guarantee. Nothing is behaving contrary to spec, so this is a gap and not a bug. A candidate replacement metric is in-band quality rather than level - voice-band-to-hiss ratio, or the 3-8 Hz syllabic modulation ratio, which measured 1.52 on this segment against a >2 expectation for clean speech. NOT changed yet: one observation is not enough to retune a load-bearing gate, and the corpus now exists to measure it properly.

TUNING finding 2026-09-07: on Parker's rig the segmenter hysteresis window straddles squelch-open hiss, so one spoken transmission became a 59-second segment. Measured levels around the 13:59 broadcast: -40.7 dBFS before, -19 during, then -36.4 for fifteen seconds AFTER the voice stopped - the radio stays unmuted with hiss. close_threshold_db is -38.1, BELOW that hiss, so once the gate opens it cannot close until the squelch itself closes. open_threshold_db (-34.1) is correctly ABOVE the hiss, so hiss alone will not start a segment. The root of it: calibrate.py measures the squelch-CLOSED line (-41.1), but this rig has a third level calibration never sees - squelch-open hiss at about -36.4 - and any close threshold below it holds segments open. Raising close to about -35.5 would close promptly but leaves only ~1.4 dB of hysteresis, which carries its own risk. NOT changed yet; one observation is not enough, and the effect is inflated segment duration plus trailing hiss fed to ASR rather than lost detections.

RESOLVED 2026-09-07 by moving the radio from the desk into the WINDOW - nothing else changed. Capture went from 1-of-8 to 6-of-6 against a human listening on an identical radio. The diagnosis chain below is kept because the reasoning matters and several hypotheses were wrong: both radios are the same model with squelch fixed in the codeplug by the fire department communications chief (Parker may not change it) and they were SIDE BY SIDE during the morning traffic, which eliminated siting, model, squelch programming, tone squelch and channel. The leading hypothesis had become computer RFI desensing the radio through the audio cable; that is now unlikely, because the audio noise floor barely moved between positions (-38.1 desk to -37.7 window) while reception transformed. It was position: at VHF a few feet and a window frame is enough. TWO RESIDUAL PROBLEMS remain. (1) Two of the six transmissions arrived as 0.2 s blips and were discarded by min_duration_ms=600, one of them the only distress-adjacent traffic of the day (towing a boat taking on water); loosening min_duration would not help, since the squelch opened and shut and there are only 0.2 s of audio - marginal signals are still lost and the loss is silent. (2) Every strong capture now CLIPS at peak_dbfs 0.2, which is newly cheap to fix: speech lands at -8.7 to -10.5 dBFS RMS against a -38 floor, 28 dB of SNR, so the radio volume can drop ~10 dB (17 to about 13-14) and still leave 18 dB of margin. The window position is currently held by nothing but memory and should be physically marked. ORIGINAL DIAGNOSIS: MEASURED 2026-09-07, and it reframes what limits this rig: the radio's SQUELCH is the real detection threshold, not open_threshold_db. Over 30.3 minutes the voice band shows exactly one event (10:44:23, lifting 44.9 dB above the floor); the next largest thing in the whole recording lifts 3.8 dB for 0.1 s, which is noise. Nothing exists in between. That bimodality is squelch behaving as a hard RF gate - a signal either breaks it and arrives fully quieting, or the audio output stays muted and NOTHING reaches the capture chain. It is why the event count is identical at floor+4 and floor+10 dB: every threshold across a 40 dB range performs the same because there is no signal population in that range to discriminate. Two consequences. (1) D19's +7-vs-+10 threshold reasoning is largely moot on this rig - keep the setting, but it does not buy the sensitivity that argument implied. (2) The operator heard 3 transmissions by ear on a second radio (10:31, 10:38, 10:44) and the rig captured 1; the two misses contain no signal at all in the recording (voice-band excursion 0.6 and 2.8 dB across +/-90 s), so they were lost at the RF stage and NO software change recovers them. Confound to resolve: the second radio is a different receiver, possibly better sited or with different squelch, so part of the gap may be that rather than the antenna - the clean test is both radios side by side. This makes the antenna the measured top priority rather than the theoretical one. ORIGINAL NOTE: Ch 16 IS receivable at Parker's site, unlike Andy's - confirmed 2026-09-07 by a 30-minute recording that captured one real marine transmission at 10:44:23 PDT, strong enough to clip. This is the first marine corpus audio the project has, and it unblocks marine corpus collection at this location. CORRECTED 2026-09-07, same day: the earlier reading of 'traffic volume is very low' was WRONG and must not be used for the Phase 4 watchdog threshold. A second 20-minute session (11:45-12:05 PDT) recorded ZERO events - largest voice-band excursion 4.4 dB against 44.9 dB for a real transmission - while the operator listening on a second handheld at the same site (Parker's FIRE STATION - all Parker/UFO202 sessions are there, not a home) logged FIVE transmissions in four minutes (11:47-11:50), including a readable exchange with a vessel identifying as Corvesta. The site has ample Ch 16 traffic; the monitoring receiver cannot hear it. Note which transmission the rig DID catch this morning: the one that arrived hot enough to CLIP at 0 dBFS. The rig appears to receive only signals strong enough to overload the input, which is a large sensitivity deficit rather than a weak-signal edge case - the 11:48-11:50 transmissions were readable by ear and still produced nothing. The audio chain is eliminated as a cause: the recording floor is -38.1 dBFS, matching every session with the radio connected, versus -88.8 with the UFO202's inputs open, so cable, interface, host, capture code and thresholds are all fine and the fault is entirely upstream of the audio. Candidates, now reordered after further analysis. (1) PROGRAMMED SQUELCH LEVEL - the leading hypothesis. 'No accessible squelch control' has been read throughout these docs as 'squelch is not adjustable', which is wrong for a commercial radio: on the NX-5000 series squelch level is a per-channel parameter in the CODEPLUG, not a knob. A tight programmed squelch on Ch 16 would produce exactly the observed behaviour - silence for everything except an overwhelming local station. Free immediate test: most Kenwood commercial portables have a Monitor / squelch-off side key that forces squelch open. Press it during traffic. Rushing noise THEN transmissions means squelch level is the fault and it is a programming change (hardware.md 3.6 already treats squelch-open as a deliberate option); rushing noise and nothing else means RF is not reaching the radio and the antenna/position is next. (2) antenna not seated, damaged or missing; (3) position and shielding - the monitoring radio sits beside a laptop, dock and USB supplies while the operator's other radio moves around; (4) a CTCSS/DCS receive tone on Ch 16, confirmed absent on Andy's radio but NEVER confirmed on Parker's; (5) wrong channel or zone. Candidate 4 is weakened but not excluded by the 10:44 capture. Supporting evidence that this is longstanding behaviour rather than a regression: across both sessions the operator heard 8 transmissions by ear and the rig captured 1, and the one it caught arrived hot enough to CLIP. The two sessions are also spectrally IDENTICAL - same mains-dominant idle signature, same band rolloff, same DC, same peak character - so nothing in the chain changed between them. A third scan ran Whisper over the entire 20-minute empty session in 30 s chunks normalised to near full scale and found ZERO speech segments, which is telling because Whisper is documented in this project as hallucinating readily on noise; it produced nothing at all. Finally, the physics rules out 'faint speech under the noise': FM squelch is binary and the AF level is set by the volume control, not by signal strength, so a weak station gives full-level scratchy audio rather than quiet audio. Absence of audio therefore means the squelch never opened, not that the signal was too quiet to record. The decisive test is free: both radios side by side in the same spot during traffic, then swap antennas between them. This is hardware.md section 5 step 1, still unticked on BOTH rigs after two sessions, and it is exactly the situation that step exists to prevent.

FIXED 2026-09-07 by dropping the radio volume 17 -> 13 of 0-31 and recalibrating (floor -41.1, thresholds -34.1/-38.1). Verified against 2h14m of real traffic: 49 clipped samples in an 18 s event (0.006%) versus 2844 and 6698 (~1%) at volume 17, a ~150x reduction, with speech peaking at -9.9 dBFS RMS and 24 dB of margin over the gate. Capture rate did NOT suffer: the transmissions missed in that session show voice-band lifts of 1.4-4.5 dB against a 4.4 dB noise ceiling measured on a definitively empty session, so the audio never arrived and the squelch never opened. ORIGINAL REPORT: Parker's rig CLIPS on real strong traffic: the 2026-09-07 Ch 16 transmission hit 0.00 dBFS with 6698 clipped samples (1.16% of the window). The level was set against a ch 7 test transmission peaking at -9.2 dBFS, which was not the loudest signal the system would see - hardware.md 3.5 warns about exactly this and Andy avoided it by calibrating against a nearby radio at full quieting. The bind is that this rig cannot simply turn the radio down: the noise enters DOWNSTREAM of the volume knob (D19), so lowering the knob drops signal while the floor stays put, costing SNR at the quiet end where this rig already has none to spare. Clipping happens at the UFO202's ADC and the radio's volume is the only control upstream of it, so there is no other stage to use. This makes the undiagnosed ~43 dB noise problem a concrete capability cost rather than an untidy number: with Andy's 60 dB of range both headroom and sensitivity fit, with Parker's ~30 dB they do not.

Marine Ch 16 is not receivable at the POC site (Andy's house, stock rubber duck indoors), confirming the hardware.md 4 warning. The system cannot currently do its actual job at this location no matter how well the pipeline works. Highest-value fix is an antenna (telescopic whip or mag-mount + SMA adapter, in a window with a view of the water), or recording the marine corpus somewhere better sited.

Segmenter verification will run against strong rebroadcast fire traffic, not marine traffic. This validates segmentation LOGIC (thresholds, hang time, pre-roll, fragmentation) but NOT weak-signal sensitivity: a central-station rebroadcast arrives fully quieting while a distant vessel does not. Do not promote 'segmentation works' to 'we would hear a mayday'. Also note 'mayday' is standard fireground vocabulary for a firefighter in trouble, so watchword hits on this corpus are not false positives in the marine sense, and the marine-loaded ASR initial_prompt may hurt WER here.
